description.value: A resting-state fMRI study used group independent component analysis and time-varying functional connectivity analysis to investigate brain connectivity states and connectivity abnormalities in children with autism spectrum disorder compared with typically developing children.

spans.text: To investigate the influence of ASD on brain connectivity states, we performed group independent component analysis (GICA) and dynamic network analysis on fMRI data of ASD and TD children.

value: ASD could influence time-varying functional connectivity states through affecting distribution of connectivity strength and influence the connectivities related to social function.

spans.text: We hypothesized that ASD could influence time-varying functional connectivity states through affecting distribution of connectivity strength and influence the connectivities related to social function.

model_settings.value: Infomax algorithm; ICA model order 100; PCA dimension reduction; ICASSO repetition 25 times; k-means clustering with Manhattan distance, k ranging from 2 to 20 and 150 repetitions per k.
